rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for an additional or greater amount, including when the noun is understood.

example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jiu3 do1 di1 faan6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for a greater or additional quantity, as in 多啲繃帶.

example.english: Could you add more salt to this soup?
example.traditional: 呢個湯可唔可以加多啲鹽？
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 tong1 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gaa1 do1 di1 jim4

rows.note: Use this when saying that additional items are still available or exist, as in 仲有繃帶.

example.english: There is more beer in the fridge.
example.jyutping: syut3 gwai6 jap6 min6 zung6 jau5 be1 zau2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken pattern for making an adjective or adverb comparative, as in 靚啲 “more beautiful.”

example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 peng4 di1

rows.note: Use this for a greater amount or degree, especially after a verb or predicate, and for an incremental comparison.
Use this when “more” has an emphatic or “even more” sense, usually in an explicit comparison.

example.english: Today is even more chilly than yesterday.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 zung6 dung3 gwo3 kam4 jat6
